lens: Jung/Pauli-inspired observation-map, selection-bias and null-record review plus occult/mystical/government source reading by a model agent; no historical-person participation or endorsement
verification_method: Quotations were located in raw OCR/HTML/PDF text downloaded locally (curl or stream extraction) and are not taken from fetch-tool summaries, which truncate long pages; entries marked 'via fetch' are abstract-level or targeted-section reads mediated by the tool and are labelled as such.
scope: Bounded selected reading of seven new historical/occult/government items plus leads, and eleven 2024-2026 technical items; not a complete corpus or literature survey.

sources.title: Synchronicity: An Acausal Connecting Principle (in The Interpretation of Nature and the Psyche)
sources.author: C. G. Jung; tr. R. F. C. Hull
sources.version_date: Bollingen Series LI, Pantheon Books, copyright 1955 (German original 1952); archive.org OCR, upload date not shown
sources.section: Ch. 1 pp. 12, 24-26, 36; Ch. 2 'An Astrological Experiment' pp. 60-92; Editors' appendix to ch. 2 (Fierz) p. 92
sources.reading_depth: Raw OCR downloaded (435k chars) and searched; the cited sentences read in context; whole essay not read; German original not collated
sources.provenance: Digitized authenticated Bollingen edition (OCR, moderate quality)
sources.claim: Jung defines synchronicity as 'a coincidence in time of two or more causally unrelated events which have the same or a similar meaning'; his astrological marriage experiment grew from a 180-pair pilot to 483 marriages; maxima were selected among fifty aspects after tabulation; the mathematician's probability (Fierz) was 1:10,000, corrected to 1:1500 and corrected again; Jung records that 'the average frequency of 10% ... is far from representing a significant figure' and 'The errors all tend to exaggerate the results in a way favourable to astrology'.
sources.historical_assertion: Synchronicity is an acausal ordering principle of nature; ESP 'cannot be a phenomenon of force or energy'.
sources.physical_claim_status: Not admitted. The text is used only as a documented record of post-hoc selection, growing batches, recomputed probabilities and experimenter expectation.
sources.relevance: Direct template for Round32 pre-registration rules R1-R4: freeze observable and threshold before outcomes; report every batch; pilot data excluded from the counted result.
sources.unresolved_verification: Page numbers taken from OCR running heads; the 1952 German text and the CW 8 revision were not compared.

sources.title: The Influence of Archetypal Ideas on the Scientific Theories of Kepler (in The Interpretation of Nature and the Psyche)
sources.author: W. Pauli; tr. Priscilla Silz
sources.version_date: Bollingen Series LI, Pantheon Books, 1955 (German original 1952)
sources.section: pp. 193-194 (Fludd's harmonic table; Kepler's criterion of objective science), pp. 205-206 (quaternary vs trinitarian attitudes), pp. 208-210 (complementarity, psyche/physis), pp. 227-233 (Fludd excerpt incl. Dee's hieroglyphic monad, p. 232)
sources.reading_depth: Raw OCR searched; cited passages read in context; essay not read in full; footnoted Latin sources not checked against Fludd's originals
sources.claim: Pauli reads the Kepler-Fludd polemic as quantitative/trinitarian versus symbolic/quaternary attitudes; states 'According to Kepler ... only that which is capable of quantitative, mathematical proof belongs to objective science, the rest is personal'; closes with 'It would be most satisfactory of all if physis and psyche could be seen as complementary aspects of the same reality. We do not yet know, however ...'.
sources.historical_assertion: Archetypal ideas act as ordering factors between sense perception and concepts in theory formation.
sources.physical_claim_status: Not admitted; Pauli's closing is a surmise he explicitly leaves open. No observer or consciousness variable follows.
sources.relevance: Supports the labelling discipline (symbolism vs proof) and warns against reading an analogy as a mechanism.
sources.unresolved_verification: Semantic Scholar/Springer/Routledge reprints exist but were not compared; the 1952 German text not collated.

sources.title: Ioannis Keppleri Harmonices Mundi Libri V (with Appendix comparing Ptolemy and Robert Fludd)
sources.author: Johannes Kepler
sources.version_date: Linz 1619 (Smithsonian Libraries / Burndy copy; second copy Royal Library Copenhagen); OCR
sources.section: Book V ch. III prop. XIII ('proportio mediorum motuum ... est sesquialtera eversa proportionis orbium', back-reference 'per VIII. praemissum'); ch. IV opening null statement 'Non deprehenditur igitur Creator Deus inter has morarum summas collectas in Tempora periodica, voluisse introducere proportiones harmonicas'; ch. IV Tycho passage ('per accuratissimas Tychonis Brahei observationes ... septendecim annorum studio'); Appendix p. 253 on Fludd ('meri Symbolismi ... poeticos potius esse aut oratorios, quam philosophicos aut mathematicos')
sources.reading_depth: Both OCR texts downloaded (about 1.0M chars each) and searched; the four passages read with OCR long-s normalized by the reader; Book V prop. VIII (the third-law sentence with 'certissima exactissimaque') NOT located in either OCR; no modern translation consulted
sources.provenance: Digitized 1619 print (public domain); OCR quality moderate to poor
sources.claim: Kepler records that harmonic proportions are not found in the periodic times (null), places them in extreme angular velocities, anchors intervals in Tycho's observations, and dismisses Fludd's harmonies as symbolisms rather than mathematics.
sources.historical_assertion: The Creator introduced harmonic proportions into planetary motions.
sources.physical_claim_status: Not admitted as such; the 3/2 power law survives as an empirical regularity; the harmonic archetype does not.
sources.relevance: Historical precedent for recording a null result and for labelling a symbolic claim as non-mathematical; used for translation T2 and rule R8.
sources.unresolved_verification: The specific third-law sentence remains unverified from the primary print in this pass; the Latin reconstructions from OCR should be checked against the Gesammelte Werke edition.

sources.title: Monas Hieroglyphica ('The Hieroglyphic Monad')
sources.author: John Dee; tr. J. W. Hamilton-Jones (1947)
sources.version_date: Antwerp 1564; Hamilton-Jones translation 1947; Esoteric Archives (J. H. Peterson) web edition, page date not shown
sources.section: Theorems I, II, III, VI, VII, X
sources.reading_depth: Raw HTML downloaded and the quoted theorems located; the dedication (omitted by the translator) and later theorems not read; Latin original not consulted
sources.provenance: Translation of a primary occult text hosted on an amateur scholarly archive; translator's omissions noted on the page
sources.claim: 'It is by the straight line and the circle that the first and most simple example and representation of all things may be demonstrated' (I); 'by virtue of the point and the Monad that all things commence to emerge in principle' (II); ternary/quaternary from lines (VI); 'this a man learns by experiment' (VII); separation 'by the application of Fire' (X).
sources.historical_assertion: A geometric symbol encodes number, astronomy and alchemical transformation.
sources.relevance: Interpretation only; historically linked to Fludd's argument reproduced in Pauli's essay (p. 232).
sources.unresolved_verification: Fidelity of the 1947 translation to the 1564 Latin not checked.

sources.title: Three Books of Occult Philosophy, Book II, ch. I-III
sources.author: Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa; tr. J.F. (1651); digital edition J. H. Peterson (2000)
sources.section: Ch. I 'Of the necessity of Mathematicall learning'; ch. II 'Of Numbers, and of their power, and vertue'; ch. III 'How great vertues Numbers have'
sources.reading_depth: Raw HTML downloaded and chapter openings located and read; remainder of Book II not read; Latin original not consulted
sources.provenance: Early-modern English translation of a primary occult text on an amateur scholarly archive
sources.claim: 'The Doctrines of Mathematicks are so necessary to, and have such an affinity with Magick ...'; 'all things ... seem to be formed by the proportion of numbers, for this was the principall pattern in the mind of the Creator'; virtues of numbers asserted on the authority of philosophers and church fathers.
sources.historical_assertion: Number is the pattern of creation and has efficacy.
sources.physical_claim_status: Not admitted; evidence offered is testimony and anecdote.
sources.relevance: Template of number-first reasoning (3-6-9, golden ratio) that the panel rules exclude from Hamiltonians.
sources.unresolved_verification: None needed for its use here.

sources.version_date: Theosophical Publishing House 1919; Project Gutenberg eBook 16058, released 2005-06-14

sources.title: An Evaluation of Remote Viewing: Research and Applications
sources.author: Michael D. Mumford, Andrew M. Rose, David A. Goslin (American Institutes for Research)
sources.version_date: 29 September 1995; declassified copy hosted by the National Security Archive (GWU); CIA document number CIA-RDP96-00791R000200180006-4 per search metadata
sources.section: Title page; Executive Summary E-1 to E-5; ch. 2 'Evaluation Plan' pp. 2-1 to 2-5; ch. 3 opening; ch. 5 conclusions
sources.reading_depth: PDF downloaded through the fetch tool and its uncompressed text streams extracted locally (387k chars); the cited sentences read in context; Utts and Hyman chapters not read in full
sources.provenance: Government-commissioned evaluation report in declassified custody (CIA FOIA; NSA Archive copy). Two CIA Reading Room locators redirected to the homepage, so CIA custody is recorded from metadata only.
sources.claim: 'A statistically significant laboratory effort has been demonstrated in the sense that hits occur more often than chance'; 'Use of the same remote viewers, the same judge, and the same target photographs makes it impossible to identify their independent effects'; 'In no case had the information provided ever been used to guide intelligence operations'; 'continued use of remote viewing in intelligence gathering operations is not warranted'; 'the two reviewers agreed far more than they disagreed'; 'both reviewers stress the need for independent replication'.
sources.historical_assertion: A laboratory anomaly was recorded; its cause was not demonstrated; the program had no operational value.
sources.physical_claim_status: Not admitted. Government custody is provenance; the report's own conclusion is negative on use.
sources.relevance: The shared-judge/shared-target confound is the same-author and shared-premise problem of paired production; supports rule R6.
sources.unresolved_verification: The CIA-hosted copy was not retrieved; the NSA Archive copy and a third-party transcription agree on the quoted sentences.
